_comment: Is this task specification actually testable, before anything is
`agentctl task validate` already checks a spec's structure - required
fields, known skills, well-formed path globs. Structure is not the thing
that wastes a budget. A spec that is complete and well-formed but whose
acceptance criteria say 'the feed should feel responsive' sends the test
agent to write tests against nothing, and the cost of finding that out is
the full three attempts plus a Manager call.
This runs once per task, before DISPATCH_TEST_AGENT, and costs a fraction
of a cent. It is the cheapest gate in the system by a wide margin.
It gates dispatch; it never edits the spec. Only the Director changes a
task contract (.ai/prompts/manager.md), and that stays true here.

testability.instructions: The state contains a task specification for an automated coding workflow: its description, its acceptance criteria, and the paths it is permitted to change. A test agent will read this and must write failing tests that pin the required behaviour BEFORE any implementation exists. Grade how well the acceptance criteria support that.
testability.legend: testable: each acceptance criterion names an observable behaviour with a determinable pass/fail outcome. underspecified: the intent is clear but at least one criterion leaves the expected result, the inputs, or the boundary conditions unstated, so a test author would have to guess. untestable: the criteria are subjective, self-contradictory, or describe no observable behaviour at all.

paths_sufficient.instructions: Could the acceptance criteria be satisfied entirely within the paths this task is permitted to change? Answer false if satisfying them would clearly require editing a file outside those paths.
paths_sufficient._why: The permission model refuses out-of-scope writes at guard time, by which point an attempt has already been spent. A spec whose criteria cannot be met inside its own allowed_paths is a Director error, and catching it before dispatch costs nothing.

testability._why: Not 'testable': an unsure grader must not wave a task through. 'underspecified' routes to a human, who spends a minute, rather than to the test agent, which would spend the budget.

paths_sufficient._why: True on low confidence, so an uncertain answer does not block a legitimate task on a question the model could not read well. The guard still enforces the real boundary at commit time - this question is an early warning, not the control.
